chunks: Ahmad ibn Isha narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Karkhi who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), 'When does the time for Dhuhr prayer enter?' He said, 'When the sun passes its zenith.' I said, 'When does its time exit?' He said, 'After four spans (of time) have passed from its zenith. Indeed, the time for Dhuhr is narrow, unlike other times.' I said, 'When does the time for Asr prayer enter?' He said, 'Indeed, the end of the time for Dhuhr is the beginning of the time for Asr.' I said, 'When does the time for Asr exit?' He said, 'The time for Asr is until the sun sets, and that is with an excuse, and it is considered neglect.' I said to him, 'If a man prayed Dhuhr after four spans had passed from the sun's zenith, would it not be considered fulfilled in your view?' He said, 'If he did so deliberately to contradict the Sunnah and the prescribed time, it would not be accepted from him, just as if a man delayed Asr until close to sunset deliberately without an excuse, it would not be accepted from him. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) has set times for the obligatory prayers and defined their limits in his Sunnah for the people. So whoever shows preference away from one of his obligatory Sunnahs is like one who shows preference away from the obligations of Allah, the Exalted.'

As for what he mentioned (may Allah have mercy on him) regarding the consideration of the zenith using the astrolabe and the geometric circle, the reference in that is to the experts, and it is not taken from the perspective of the text (hadith). As for the consideration using the upright stick (gnomon)...

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ: Four spans (a traditional unit of time measurement)
key_terms.الضَّيْقُ: Narrow (referring to the limited duration of Dhuhr time)
key_terms.تَضْيِيعٌ: Neglect (referring to delaying prayer until the last moment)
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: Solar zenith (when the sun passes its highest point)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific start and end times for Dhuhr and Asr prayers according to Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential boundaries of Dhuhr and Asr, emphasizing that the narrowness of Dhuhr is a distinct legal characteristic rather than a general rule. It highlights the Shia principle that deliberate deviation from the Prophet's established timings without valid excuse invalidates the prayer, equating such negligence with neglecting obligatory duties. The text also notes the scholarly distinction between textual evidence and astronomical instruments like the astrolabe for determining solar zenith.
